1239|c86281a7.name: First Mate Fitzsimmons
1239|c86281a7.text: If you're willing to endure tales that will shiver your timbers and sog your skivvies, then get yourself a drink and sit for a spell...

1287|ed056522.name: Marda Weller
1287|ed056522.text: Best deals in all of Stormwind my friend, won't find any better. Now, what can I help you with?

1287|fe52f4ea.name: Marda Weller
1287|fe52f4ea.text: Just browsing my wares or is there something specific I can help you find today?

1299|fe52f4ea.name: Lisbeth Schneider
1299|fe52f4ea.text: Just browsing my wares or is there something specific I can help you find today?

1314|0624ab70.name: Duncan Cullen
1314|0624ab70.text: Since the fall of Dalaran and the destruction of Quel'Thalas, wares of this sort have been hard to come by. But Lucan Cordell and some of our other Tradesman have been doing a fine job of filling our orders with quality merchandise.

14450|d3e1a5a0.name: Orphan Matron Nightingale
14450|d3e1a5a0.text:
There are costs with war, $c... ones often overlooked.  Those costs are the orphans - children who have lost their parents to the far-too-numerous conflicts that rage across Azeroth.  Those children who have no one else to turn to often come here to live until they are old enough to fend for themselves.

One week out of the year during the Spring, the Alliance takes time to give something back to these innocents.  This time is called Children's Week.

1464|b63e4e81.name: Innkeeper Helbrek
1464|b63e4e81.text: Fill yer tankard and pull up a chair. We've stories to tell and kegs to empty.

1571|c5ceacbe.name: Shellei Brondir
1571|c5ceacbe.text: Where would you like to fly to?

1573|10cfc531.name: Gryth Thurden
1573|10cfc531.text: The Wildhammer dwarves might have fast steeds, but can those Aerie Peak gryphons stand the heat of The Great Forge?  I think not!

1719|bf4c7bb7.name: Warden Thelwater
1719|bf4c7bb7.text: Over here, you worthless...! If you want to do something useful, listen quick!

2409|c5ceacbe.name: Felicia Maline
2409|c5ceacbe.text: Where would you like to fly to?

2455|105cd232.name: Olivia Burnside
2455|105cd232.text: No one's ever stolen anything out of here. Not in the whole history of... the whole history!

2455|2237a3b1.name: Olivia Burnside
2455|2237a3b1.text: Welcome to the Bank of Stormwind. We offer financial accounts and safety deposit boxes for valuable items. Do you already have an account with us sir?

256390|6a190ff9.name: Marcy Baker
256390|6a190ff9.text: We've had trouble with shipments going missing across Azeroth. If you find any, I'd appreciate if you could return them to me.

256735|8db10840.name: Mivin Shadowweave
256735|8db10840.text: <Mivin gestures toward his wares and back at you again with a smile, but says nothing.>

258785|726390d0.name: High Priestess Mims
258785|726390d0.text: Surrender to the Light, $N. How can I help you serve today?

265|94d9e780.name: Madame Eva
265|94d9e780.text: I have sensed your coming for quite some time, $N.  It was written in the pattern of the stars.

268|f1060a41.name: Sirra Von'Indi
268|f1060a41.text: Greetings, $c! I have but one goal: the cataloging and recording of all knowledge related to the history of Duskwood and Darkshire. Perhaps you could help me in my endeavor?

27305|3d2da9f9.name: Argent Healer
27305|3d2da9f9.text: Do not lose hope, my son.  With faith, we will march  through this darkness and once again see the dawn.

278680|fe2e6e48.name: Gabbi Goodwhistle
278680|fe2e6e48.text: What can I do for ya?

352|4946c28b.name: Dungar Longdrink
352|4946c28b.text: Where is it ye would like to go lad? For just a few coin my Gryphons can get ye there faster than even the swiftest horse.

352|c23f1156.name: Dungar Longdrink
352|c23f1156.text: These great beasts know paths that ye can't find on foot, they'll get ye there fast and maybe show ye something new at the same time.

376|bab8ec77.name: High Priestess Laurena
376|bab8ec77.text: I trust the Light is with you, $N. Is there something that I can I help you with?

523|d6469a91.name: Thor
523|d6469a91.text: Where are you going?  Well if you're looking to get there quickly, then look no further!

5567|3a20317a.name: Sellandus
5567|3a20317a.text: A fine display of worthiness. Your instruction may now continue.

6740|c80041d2.name: Innkeeper Allison
6740|c80041d2.text: Welcome to my Inn, weary traveler. What can I do for you?

6790|c80041d2.name: Innkeeper Trelayne
6790|c80041d2.text: Welcome to my Inn, weary traveler. What can I do for you?

7766|2849f8e9.name: Tyrion
7766|2849f8e9.text:
You'll have to be patient with me, $N. I've got my Spybot inside working on a very delicate matter. I'll be with ya in a second.

Oh, and do me a favor, try not to let Lescovar see you... we're about to ambush him.

928|837f02f9.name: Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker
928|837f02f9.text: May the Light protect you this day.

931|c5ceacbe.name: Ariena Stormfeather
931|c5ceacbe.text: Where would you like to fly to?

1241-accept.name: Bishop DeLavey
1241-accept.text:
Recently a diplomat was sent to Theramore to meet with Jaina Proudmoore. That diplomat never arrived.

I believe the Defias are involved in this plot, but I'm not sure how. The diplomat's disappearance still eludes public attention, but it can't remain that way for long.

Agents of the king are already scouring the city for clues, but I have my own contacts I would like involved.

In the Valley of Heroes is an old friend of mine named Jorgen. Find him, give him this note, and follow his instructions.
1241-accept.title: The Missing Diplomat

1274-accept.name: Thomas
1274-accept.text:
Excuse me, sir. Bishop DeLavey asked me to approach adventurers that might be able to help him with a delicate matter.

If you could quietly head to Stormwind Keep and speak to him at your earliest convenience, I'm sure he would appreciate your help. Again, please be discreet. It is a matter of some importance.
1274-accept.title: The Missing Diplomat

1274-complete.name: Bishop DeLavey
1274-complete.text:
Hello, $N. I am Bishop DeLavey.

No doubt if you're asking me about my business here in the keep then young Thomas has succeeded in requisitioning you to help our kingdom. He has always been adept at following my requests.

I'm afraid I don't have time to elaborate much, so allow me to be blunt... and please, try to keep this from becoming common knowledge.
1274-complete.title: The Missing Diplomat

133-accept.name: Abercrombie
133-accept.text:
I live so far from the protection of town, it's a wonder the ghouls and the walking dead haven't eaten me!  In fact, just yesterday a pack of Bone Chewers was pounding on the walls of my house!

I want to make an effigy - a kind of "scarecrow" for Ghouls.  To do that I need some Ghoul Ribs.  You can get them from Flesh Eaters, Bone Chewers, Brain Eaters, Rotted Ones and Plague Spreaders.

Get the ribs for me, and I will repay you with some coin.
133-accept.title: Ghoulish Effigy

133-complete.name: Abercrombie
133-complete.text: Ah, thanks.  These will do just the trick!
133-complete.title: Ghoulish Effigy

133-progress.name: Abercrombie
133-progress.text: I think I hear a pack of Ghouls scurrying around the back of the house - I better put that effigy up quick!  Did you get those Ghoul Ribs for me?
133-progress.title: Ghoulish Effigy

134-accept.name: Abercrombie
134-accept.text:
A few weeks ago I was picking herbs far from my house, and a band of ogres attacked me!  I ran, and I was forced to leave behind a crate of precious tools and herbs.

After they chased me off, the ogres swaggered back to the ogre mound in southern Duskwood.  I'm sure my crate is somewhere near the mound.

Please, $N, retrieve this crate for me for I miss it sorely.
134-accept.title: Ogre Thieves

134-complete.name: Abercrombie
134-complete.text:
Thank the Nec-...well, thank YOU, $N!  You have more than earned your reward.

Aha!  Happy!  Happy nights ahead!!
134-complete.title: Ogre Thieves

134-progress.name: Abercrombie
134-progress.text: Do you have my crate?  If so, then please...give it to me quickly!
134-progress.title: Ogre Thieves

149-complete.name: Blind Mary
149-complete.text:
What is this?  A comb?  It's lovely!  And it glides through my hair as if it weren't the stiff, stringy horror that it is.

Oh, if only I had a mirror...
149-complete.title: Ghost Hair Thread

149-progress.name: Blind Mary
149-progress.text:
<Sob> Oh please, don't look at me!  I tore out these eyes with my own hands, but I can still feel your gaze!

I'm hideous!  Hideous!  Please, look away!!
149-progress.title: Ghost Hair Thread

154-accept.name: Blind Mary
154-accept.text:
NO!!!!!

Take it, take this comb away from me!

I'm a monster, and no one will ever think me lovely again!
154-accept.title: Return the Comb

154-complete.name: Madame Eva
154-complete.text: I can make a spool of Ghost Hair Thread with this, and have a few strands to spare.  Here are some coins for those extra strands.
154-complete.title: Return the Comb

154-progress.name: Madame Eva
154-progress.text: I sense that you have seen Blind Mary.  You have my Comb...?
154-progress.title: Return the Comb

156-accept.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
156-accept.text:
If you bring me some rot blossoms then I can brew you up a batch of zombie juice.

Rot blossoms grow in strange places.  In particular, I hear you can find them inside the skulls of Skeletal Horrors and Skeletal Fiends... not that I've gotten close enough to look!

The Raven Hill Cemetery and the Tranquil Gardens are both lousy with those skeletons.  You may as well get rid of them while you're looking for rot blossoms.  The town of Darkshire would be grateful.
156-accept.title: Gather Rot Blossoms

156-complete.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
156-complete.text:
Good,  you got the rot blossoms.  And I'll tell Althea Ebonlocke of the Night Watch that you were killing skeletons.

Keeping the people of Darkshire safe is a grim burden for the Night Watch, and news that others are helping stem the tide of fiends in Duskwood is welcome news indeed.
156-complete.title: Gather Rot Blossoms

156-progress.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
156-progress.text: Hi, $N.  Do you have those rot blossoms for me yet?
156-progress.title: Gather Rot Blossoms

157-accept.name: Madame Eva
157-accept.text: Here is your thread, $N.  It has a thousand uses, from binding evil spirits to sewing life into inanimate objects.
157-accept.title: Deliver the Thread

157-complete.name: Abercrombie
157-complete.text:
Delightful!  This will do splendidly...

Here, good $N, take this as payment for your honorable deed.
157-complete.title: Deliver the Thread

157-progress.name: Abercrombie
157-progress.text: I need to string the Ghost Hair Thread along my door and my windows to keep out unwanted spirits.  Did you get it for me?
157-progress.title: Deliver the Thread

158-accept.name: Abercrombie
158-accept.text:
I need a bottle of a certain liquor - Zombie Juice.  Tavernkeep Smitts at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire should have some.

And please hurry, $N.  These nights get cold, and I need that drink to put fire in my veins again!
158-accept.title: Zombie Juice

158-complete.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
158-complete.text: You need some Zombie Juice, do you?  Hmm...that's some strong stuff - I don't usually get requests for it.
158-complete.title: Zombie Juice

159-accept.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
159-accept.text:
Here's your Zombie Juice...

...and be careful with this stuff.  It's strong enough to raise the dead!
159-accept.title: Juice Delivery

159-complete.name: Abercrombie
159-complete.text:
A thousand thanks, $N.  You warm an old man's heart with your foolish-...I mean...with your kindness!

Here you are, friend.  Take this as a token of my gratitude.
159-complete.title: Juice Delivery

159-progress.name: Abercrombie
159-progress.text: I need that Zombie Juice to keep me warm on these cold, dark nights.  Did you get it for me?
159-progress.title: Juice Delivery

160-accept.name: Abercrombie
160-accept.text:
Take this note to Ello Ebonlocke, the Mayor of Darkshire.

He and I are old friends...and when he reads it and discovers what you did for me...I'm sure he'll be just as happy as I am!  Hahahaha!
160-accept.title: Note to the Mayor

160-complete.name: Lord Ello Ebonlocke
160-complete.text:
<Ello looks at the letter...>

What language is this?  It looks ancient...I can't read it.
160-complete.title: Note to the Mayor

160-progress.name: Lord Ello Ebonlocke
160-progress.text:
Abercrombie...?  I don't know a person of that name.  You say you have a letter for me from this Abercrombie fellow?

Well let's have it then...
160-progress.title: Note to the Mayor

173-complete.name: Calor
173-complete.text:
Impressive, $N. It would seem that you are capable enough to handle yourself. Perhaps a more suitable challenge could be found for one of your abilities.

It is curious though... The worgen seemed to just appear out of thin air. But then, with all the other strange creatures that have moved across our borders, I suppose it's only one of many concerns.
173-complete.title: Worgen in the Woods

181-complete.name: Viktori Prism'Antras
181-complete.text: At last!  The stargazing device is complete!  Thank you, $N.  Now I can continue my research. . .
181-complete.title: Look to the Stars

181-progress.name: Viktori Prism'Antras
181-progress.text: Were you able to convince Zzarc'Vul to lend us his monocle for our experiment?
181-progress.title: Look to the Stars

221-accept.name: Calor
221-accept.text:
You might have noticed some larger worgen wandering around with the Shadow Weavers in the woods? From what we can tell, these Dark Runners make up the bulk of the worgen numbers.

On my rangings, I've also noticed that they have overrun the Rotting Orchard southwest of town. These worgen are a bit tougher than the last you faced.

Be on your guard.
221-accept.title: Worgen in the Woods

221-complete.name: Calor
221-complete.text:
You performed well against the Dark Runners, $N. But it seems as though their numbers are inexhaustible. Every time we make progress, more spring up to refill their ranks.

What is the evil power that draws them here? Why have they come to disturb our unhappy realm...

I will put my faith in Master Carevin. No doubt he will get to the bottom of the problem.
221-complete.title: Worgen in the Woods

222-accept.name: Calor
222-accept.text:
Your previous accomplishments have convinced me that you are ready to take on the toughest worgen infesting the woods.

Of the worgen that have made their new home here, the Vile Fangs and the Tainted Ones have proven the most dangerous. They've settled down near some of the caves and in the mine to the south.

From far away you can even see the light from their bonfires...
222-accept.title: Worgen in the Woods

222-complete.name: Calor
222-complete.text: $N, to be honest with you, I did not believe that you would get this far, but you are clearly a $c to be reckoned with. In fact, if you wish to formally join Master Carevin's struggle, I will gladly write for you a letter of recommendation.
222-complete.title: Worgen in the Woods

223-accept.name: Calor
223-accept.text:
Here you go, $N. Bring this message to Master Carevin.

<He quickly removes a piece of faded parchment and offers it to you.>

A few more like you, and we will outnumber the Night Watch! Perhaps then we could complete the work that we few carry on today.
223-accept.title: Worgen in the Woods

223-complete.name: Jonathan Carevin
223-complete.text:
Excuse me for my cold reception, $N, but as I'm sure you can tell, I am an extremely busy man. I see that you have impressed Calor--and I assure you, that is no small feat--and that he has given his recommendation.

There are unsavory types afoot, $N, and we can use the help of all who have proven themselves. We battle against demons, the undead, and those who would provide them aid. Be vigilant, be wary, and trust none who would not give aid to our cause.

Glory under the Light.
223-complete.title: Worgen in the Woods

223-progress.name: Jonathan Carevin
223-progress.text: Yes, what is it? Make it quick, I've pressing matters to attend to.
223-progress.title: Worgen in the Woods

225-accept.name: Unknown
225-accept.text:
The weathered grave marker reads simply:

MORGAN LADIMORE

<Upon further examination, you notice that dirt over the grave has been recently disturbed, and that a good amount of the dirt seems to have been displaced...>
225-accept.title: The Weathered Grave

225-complete.name: Sirra Von'Indi
225-complete.text:
Morgan Ladimore?

Ahh, yes, of course. His was a long and sorrowful tale. I knew him, well, before he left for the war, but that was the last time I saw him. A noble and good man, he was, but he suffered a bad end.

Here, I should have something here that can tell the tale better than my own recollections...
225-complete.title: The Weathered Grave

227-accept.name: Sirra Von'Indi
227-accept.text:
<He searches through the shelves and comes up with a leatherbound book.>

If you would like to know more, you might ask Althea, she's been the one to handle the... trouble... with him of late.
227-accept.title: Morgan Ladimore

227-complete.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
227-complete.text:
Morgan Ladimore? Never heard of...

Oh, you mean Mor'Ladim! I guess you haven't heard the story?

Well, I'll give you the short version. A wandering undead calling itself Mor'Ladim has been wandering Duskwood. From what we've gathered, it appears to be the undead body of Morgan Ladimore, of whom you apparently know. He's been causing us all sorts of problems, attacking Watchmen on patrol and killing people.

<She sizes you up.>

You seem to be capable enough, maybe you could lay him to rest.
227-complete.title: Morgan Ladimore

228-accept.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
228-accept.text:
From what my scouts tell me, Mor'Ladim wanders throughout Duskwood, following a strange and meandering path through the cemetery. We buried him out past the house on the hill, you know where that is?

There isn't anything I can do to help you, but I wish you good luck.
228-accept.title: Mor'Ladim

228-complete.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
228-complete.text:
You killed him? That's no small accomplishment, $N! On behalf of the people of Darkshire and the Night Watch, I thank you.

Ah... there is one small matter, however...
228-complete.title: Mor'Ladim

228-progress.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
228-progress.text: I don't blame you if you're having trouble with him, $N. Some of our strongest Watchers have been lost to Mor'Ladim.
228-progress.title: Mor'Ladim

229-accept.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
229-accept.text:
I should have told you this earlier...

How do I put this...

Morgan may have believed that his family was all dead, but, in fact, his daughter Sarah Ladimore is now a Watcher. She's always been troubled by the... circumstances... surrounding her father's death. Perhaps you could go to bring the news to her.
229-accept.title: The Daughter Who Lived

229-complete.name: Watcher Ladimore
229-complete.text:
Yes? My father...

<Her eyes become downcast.>

I wish... there was something I could have done for him... If only I had talked to him before he...
229-complete.title: The Daughter Who Lived

230-accept.name: Unknown
230-accept.text:
Digging through the mound, you find a small, dirt-stained book.

The book has no title, but...it has information Sven would like to know.
230-accept.title: Sven's Camp

230-complete.name: Sven Yorgen
230-complete.text:
<Sven reads the book's pages, then slams it shut.>

That shadowy figure I saw was a witness to my family's death!  There are questions I'd like to ask that man...if only I knew who he was!
230-complete.title: Sven's Camp

230-progress.name: Sven Yorgen
230-progress.text: You found what??  Please, let me see it...
230-progress.title: Sven's Camp

231-accept.name: Watcher Ladimore
231-accept.text:
Here, take this and lay it on his grave. Maybe... somehow, he'll know that I'm okay, and that none of us hold him responsible for what happened.

<There are tears in her eyes now, as she slides a ring from her right hand, and presses it into your hands.>

And... thank you, $N.
231-accept.title: A Daughter's Love

231-complete.name: Unknown
231-complete.text:
<A ghostly voice sounds on the wind...>

This is...? Sarah? Could it be she's still alive? The weight is removed from my shoulders...

$N. Take my sword, Archeus. As my soul is put to rest, I have no more need for it. It was forged to do good, and though I have proved myself unworthy to hold it, perhaps you will carry on the Light through it. And keep the ring. I am no longer worthy of it.

Lys, my love...
231-complete.title: A Daughter's Love

245-complete.name: Watcher Dodds
245-complete.text: Ah! You're back. And not too much worse for wear, it'd seem. Of course, $N, the Night Watch is grateful for your work, and I did promise you a reward, so here.
245-complete.title: Eight-Legged Menaces

251-accept.name: Lord Ello Ebonlocke
251-accept.text: Take the note you gave me to Sirra Von'Indi.  He's very learned in languages and ancient arts - if anyone here can translate this message, it's he.
251-accept.title: Translate Abercrombie's Note

251-progress.name: Sirra Von'Indi
251-progress.text: A note from Abercrombie the hermit, eh?  I don't know him, though if he lives out at the graveyard then I do know his brains have rotted out!
251-progress.title: Translate Abercrombie's Note

252-accept.name: Sirra Von'Indi
252-accept.text:
Oh my!  If what is written on this note is true, then Abercrombie's done something...unspeakable.

You better bring the translated note back to Ello.

And do so quickly, for I fear a doom already lumbers toward our town...
252-accept.title: Translation to Ello

252-complete.name: Lord Ello Ebonlocke
252-complete.text:
<Ello reads the letter...and his face goes white.  He then looks at you...>

Although the aid you gave Abercrombie may have been motivated from kindness, your actions have doomed our town.

<Ello becomes lost in his thoughts...>
252-complete.title: Translation to Ello

252-progress.name: Lord Ello Ebonlocke
252-progress.text: Ah, is the note translated?  Please, let me see it...
252-progress.title: Translation to Ello

253-accept.name: Lord Ello Ebonlocke
253-accept.text:
The Embalmer is a name told in one of our children's stories.  He was a kindly alchemist, driven mad by the death of his wife, Eliza.  To restore her, he used dark magic to place his own heart within the bosom of his dead spouse.

This revived Eliza...but it cursed her with a hunger for human flesh, forcing the Embalmer to keep her buried.

His heart is his power.  Find his wife's grave, retrieve his heart, and bring it to me while it still beats.  Do this and his power will be broken.
253-accept.title: Bride of the Embalmer

253-complete.name: Lord Ello Ebonlocke
253-complete.text:
You've done it!  The magic within his heart will be proof against the Embalmer's evil, and a powerful aegis over the town of Darkshire.

You have done a great thing for our people, $N.  Your name will remain in our annals forever.
253-complete.title: Bride of the Embalmer

253-progress.name: Lord Ello Ebonlocke
253-progress.text: Have you yet found Eliza's grave?  Do you have the Embalmer's heart?
253-progress.title: Bride of the Embalmer

254-complete.name: Unknown
254-complete.text:
You dig through the semi-loose dirt over the grave...and find the remains of a coffin.

Within the coffin you can feel the vibrating scrapes of clawed fingers and the gnashing of rotted teeth...

Will you open the coffin and retrieve the Embalmer's heart?
254-complete.title: Digging Through the Dirt

262-accept.name: Sven Yorgen
262-accept.text:
I must know who was that skulker in the shadows I saw the night my family was killed!

Please, $N, you have shown your resourcefulness.  Please find that shadowy figure.  I must learn what secrets he holds!

I do not have clues that you do not already know, but here - take the book you found at my farm.  Perhaps some of the townsfolk can link this book with its owner.
262-accept.title: The Shadowy Figure

262-complete.name: Madame Eva
262-complete.text:
Hmm... Someone handled this book recently, someone who is driven by revenge.  But the impressions left on it, at least the impressions from the original owner, are faint.

I can tell, however, that the original owner of this book is not a native of Darkshire.
262-complete.title: The Shadowy Figure

262-progress.name: Madame Eva
262-progress.text: If you have something that belongs to the shadowy figure for whom you seek, then let me see it.  I may be able to divine something of its owner.
262-progress.title: The Shadowy Figure

265-accept.name: Madame Eva
265-accept.text:
Here is your book back, $N, and I bid you fortune with your search.  If you ask others in town, perhaps they can offer you more clues.

And here is one more for you - although the author of this book is a stranger to Darkshire, the book itself was purchased here.
265-accept.title: The Shadowy Search Continues

265-complete.name: Clerk Daltry
265-complete.text:
Ah, yes.  I sold this book a month ago to a shady person.  He didn't tell me his name, but he was a nervous, jittery chap, always looking over his shoulder.

I hope that helps you...
265-complete.title: The Shadowy Search Continues

265-progress.name: Clerk Daltry
265-progress.text:
Sometimes I'll sell blank books to scholars and mages, or to anyone who wants to keep a journal.

I remember well everyone to whom I sold a book within the last few months...
265-progress.title: The Shadowy Search Continues

266-accept.name: Clerk Daltry
266-accept.text:
Here is your book, and good luck with your inquiries.

You might want to expand your search to the inn.  If the person whom you seek spent time in town, then chances are someone saw him there.
266-accept.title: Inquire at the Inn

266-complete.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
266-complete.text:
Oh yeah, I remember this book.  Its owner rented a room for a few days, and spent his nights at the bar, writing.

He left town in a hurry, muttering about being hunted by...something.  Last I saw him he was heading west out of town, looking for a new spot to hide.

The first place he'd find to the west is Raven Hill...
266-complete.title: Inquire at the Inn

266-progress.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
266-progress.text:
The Scarlet Raven doesn't see the business it used to, but we still do get travelers passing through.

If you can describe the person you're looking for, maybe I'll remember him.
266-progress.title: Inquire at the Inn

268-accept.name: Jitters
268-accept.text:
The book you found was only half finished.  I had to leave it at Sven's farm when I fled there...

Here.  Take my completed journal to Sven.  It describes more fully what happened at his farm.

Although this journal has been my only company these past weeks, if giving it up keeps me from having to face Sven and his wrath, then I do it willingly!
268-accept.title: Return to Sven

268-complete.name: Sven Yorgen
268-complete.text: This journal explains much to me, and sets me on the path against the dark riders!  I have seen these riders in Duskwood, and have seen them speak with the wizard Morbent Fel, at the Forlorn Rowe.
268-complete.title: Return to Sven

268-progress.name: Sven Yorgen
268-progress.text: Did you find who the Shadowy Figure was?
268-progress.title: Return to Sven

269-accept.name: Sven Yorgen
269-accept.text:
Go to the city of Stormwind and speak with Bishop Farthing in the Cathedral of Light.  Give him Jitters' journal and tell him you mean to face Morbent Fel.

Although Stormwind has forsaken Darkshire, Farthing is a kind soul and very wise.  He may help you on your quest to save us.

Your mission is perilous, but hurry, $N.  With each passing hour, the shadows of Duskwood grow ever darker.
269-accept.title: Seeking Wisdom

269-complete.name: Bishop Farthing
269-complete.text:
<After reading the journal and hearing your intent...>

An evil taint has gained a foothold within the already beleaguered Duskwood.  I thank the Light we have a hero such as you to face it.

But you must first prepare yourself for the coming trial...for the Necromancer Morbent Fel is immensely powerful, and has cast dark enchantments about himself to protect him from physical assaults.  If you are to defeat him, you will need a weapon that is proof against these protections.
269-complete.title: Seeking Wisdom

269-progress.name: Bishop Farthing
269-progress.text: Rest, brother.  I can tell you have traveled far, and you bear a heavy burden.  Can you tell me what casts that dark shadow over you?
269-progress.title: Seeking Wisdom

270-accept.name: Bishop Farthing
270-accept.text:
Years ago, the Third Fleet of Kul'Tiras sunk along the coasts of The Wetlands, an expanse of marsh north of the Dwarven kingdom of Ironforge.  Aboard one ship was a load of Lightforge Iron.

This metal is precious to us, for items crafted from it strike with holy truth.  If you are to face Morbent Fel, then you will need such a weapon.

Go to Menethil Harbor and speak with my dwarven colleague Glorin Steelbrow.  If that lost metal can be found, he'll know where to look.
270-accept.title: The Doomed Fleet

270-complete.name: Glorin Steelbrow
270-complete.text:
Lightforge Iron is a precious metal, but it sounds like your quest is a dire one.  You've come a long way, Brother.  With luck, you might just find what you seek!

And if you do get the iron, I know who can fashion it into a weapon against this Necromancer you speak of in Duskwood.
270-complete.title: The Doomed Fleet

2745-accept.name: Elling Trias
2745-accept.text:
Hmm, an interesting tale, and not one to be taken lightly. Yeah, I can help you, but what you need to do is divvy out a form of justice that's not... legal, if you're to see this through to the end.

Lescovar and Marzon need to be dealt with, and swiftly. Do you think you're capable of such a thing?

You decide. If so, then make haste to the castle and find an old friend of mine, a $r named Tyrion. He's been watching Lescovar now for a couple weeks. He should be able to help you end this.
2745-accept.title: Infiltrating the Castle

2745-complete.name: Tyrion
2745-complete.text:
What the...?! Don't sneak up on me like that! And keep your voice down! What in the name of the Shadow are you doing sneakin' up on me for? Can't you see I'm busy, you daft fool?

What do you mean, what am I doing? I'm waiting for the next Dark Portal to open, what the heck do you think I'm doing? Speak your peace and be off with you... 'fore the guards notice the two of us hiding in the bushes together. I have a reputation to maintain.
2745-complete.title: Infiltrating the Castle

2746-accept.name: Tyrion
2746-accept.text:
Trias wants the timetable pushed up some, huh? Okay, we can do that, but I'm not ready. And know this, I'm doing the hard part, but you're the one that's going to get his hands dirty, understand? Good.

Okay, I'll need you to get me a few things before I can put my plan into effect. I got the perfect disguise that'll get Spybot past those guards.

Bring me some silk and a couple apples. The silk's up to you, but Clara's little farm right outside the city has the perfect sized apples.
2746-accept.title: Items of Some Consequence

288-accept.name: First Mate Fitzsimmons
288-accept.text:
I was once First Mate on the Wave Mistress, ship-of-the-line in the Kul Tiras Third Fleet. The Doomed Fleet. Doomed, for on its last voyage the fleet was attacked by Red Dragons. Dragons controlled by Orcs!

We didn't stand a chance against that dragonfire...and our fleet was burned and sunk off this here coast. I'm the sole survivor of those poor vessels...

...Oh, my head hammers and pounds! I'll need a fresh drink if I'm to get a handle on this hangover and continue my tale.
288-accept.title: The Third Fleet

288-complete.name: First Mate Fitzsimmons
288-complete.text: Ah! That hits the spot, and loosens the tongue. Thanks, mate!
288-complete.title: The Third Fleet

288-progress.name: First Mate Fitzsimmons
288-progress.text: Oh, I'm so very thirsty! Won't you buy a drink for this poor, pathetic fool?
288-progress.title: The Third Fleet

289-accept.name: First Mate Fitzsimmons
289-accept.text:
<Bolstered, Fitzsimmons continues his tale...>

I am the sole survivor of the ill-fated Third Fleet of Kul Tiras, wrecked off the coast to the north. But although I'm the only member of the fleet still breathing, I'm not the only one still walking about! For on one of our ships was hidden a great, and terrible treasure, and the eerie power of it keeps the souls of my brothers trapped within the ships' rotting hulls.

But if you can free some of my brothers, then perhaps you can break their curse.
289-accept.title: The Cursed Crew

294-accept.name: Ormer Ironbraid
294-accept.text:
The situation is severe, that much is for sure. When we uncovered these bones it attracted the Raptors. These filthy beasts killed my brethren and trapped me, Merrin and the poor Prospector up here.

Help clear the Wetlands of these Raptors, $N. Mottled Raptors and Mottled Screechers are just West of the bluff there. Kill 10 of each, if you can.

That will be a good start to the vengeance I have planned for them.
294-accept.title: Ormer's Revenge

299-accept.name: Prospector Whelgar
299-accept.text:
Just before the invasion I uncovered a large tablet called the Goaz Stone. The translated text breaks off in 4 places. The text speaks of a "divine plan" and a "doomed prophecy."

I fear we are running out of time. I am too old to go down and brave those beasts. But you are strong.

Scour the excavation site and uncover the 4 missing tablet fragments: Ados, Modr, Golm and Neru. Search for them in ancient artifacts or where the soil is loose. Bring them to me so I can begin unlocking the mystery!
299-accept.title: Uncovering the Past

299-complete.name: Prospector Whelgar
299-complete.text: Ah the Goaz Stone is complete! Fine work, $N. Fine work indeed. Now I can continue with the delicate translation of this Titan script. I can make out new words already! Hmm...it says here, "Old Gods... Chained Beneath the Land." This is the beginning of something epic.
299-complete.title: Uncovering the Past

299-progress.name: Prospector Whelgar
299-progress.text: Have you uncovered the four fragments yet, $N?  Ados, Modr, Golm and Neru...
299-progress.title: Uncovering the Past

321-accept.name: Glorin Steelbrow
321-accept.text:
The shipwrecks off the shore here are the doomed Third Fleet of Kul'Tiras, burned and sunk by Red Dragons during the last Great War.

The Fleet hailed from Lordaeron, but one ship, an Elvish Destroyer: Flying Osprey, was with it.  It was shipping a load of Lightforge Iron and joined the Third Fleet for protection.  Ironic that it sunk to the same dragons...

Enough history.  The Flying Osprey is wrecked to the south of Menethil Harbor.  If you find the Lightforge Iron there, bring it to me.
321-accept.title: Lightforge Iron

321-complete.name: Unknown
321-complete.text:
This chest is waterlogged, and its siding broken.  Many claw marks mar both the inside and outside of the chest...as if Murlocs have searched through it and stolen its treasure.

But tucked deep within the chest is a single Lightforge Ingot.  Unfortunately, many more will be needed if enough metal to fashion a weapon is to be gained.
321-complete.title: Lightforge Iron

322-accept.name: Glorin Steelbrow
322-accept.text:
There is a dwarven weaponsmith in the Dwarven District of Stormwind who can craft with lightforge iron.  His name is Grimand Elmore.

I've packed the iron you found into a crate.  Take it to Grimand and tell him your tale.  I'm sure he'll oblige someone on a quest such as yours, and craft for you a weapon - a weapon to give even Morbent Fel worry!
322-accept.title: Blessed Arm

323-accept.name: Sven Yorgen
323-accept.text:
Morbent Fel is a necromancer, and an ally to the dark riders.  I would pit you against the power of Morbent Fel, but I will not send you against that vile fiend without first knowing your strength.

You have already proven your bravery to me, but if you truly wish to face the necromancer, then you must now prove your skill against his minions.
323-accept.title: Proving Your Worth

323-complete.name: Sven Yorgen
323-complete.text: Your skill in combat, $N, can not be doubted.  Your resolve may yet see us through to the end of Morbent Fel!
323-complete.title: Proving Your Worth

324-accept.name: Unknown
324-accept.text: Having grabbed the single lightforge ingot from the waterlogged chest, it is clear that murlocs have stolen the rest.  Hunt the murloc raiders near the Flying Osprey wreckage for the lost lightforge iron.
324-accept.title: The Lost Ingots

324-complete.name: Glorin Steelbrow
324-complete.text: Ah, you found them!  Now let's get this lightforge iron hammered into something useful, eh?
324-complete.title: The Lost Ingots

324-progress.name: Glorin Steelbrow
324-progress.text: Did you find the lightforge iron you need?
324-progress.title: The Lost Ingots

334-accept.name: Rema Schneider
334-accept.text:
My son Thurman is an apprentice at the Larson Clothiers, in the Mage's Quarter.  He was in a hurry today and forgot his shears and needles.  I know a great $C like you must have important tasks at hand, but without his tools Thurman can't do his apprentice work!

Please, $N.  Can you take my son's sewing kit to him?  Larson Clothiers is one of two clothing shops in the Mage's Quarter - it's the one deeper in, near the Mage's Tower.
334-accept.title: Package for Thurman

334-complete.name: Thurman Schneider
334-complete.text:
Oh, blast!  I thought forgetting my kit would free me from work.  Now I guess I'll have to help the Larsons with their sewing...

Oh, well.  Fun will come later I guess.
334-complete.title: Package for Thurman

334-progress.name: Thurman Schneider
334-progress.text: Are you here to buy clothes?
334-progress.title: Package for Thurman

337-complete.name: Milton Sheaf
337-complete.text:
Oh my!  This book hasn't rested on these shelves since before the rebuilding of Stormwind, years ago.  It will have to be restored of course, it's in bad shape, but I would be honored to place it within our rare books collection.

Thank you, sir.  Please accept this as payment for returning the book!
337-complete.title: An Old History Book

337-progress.name: Milton Sheaf
337-progress.text: Ooh!  What's that old book you have there?  Can I see it??
337-progress.title: An Old History Book

350-accept.name: Master Mathias Shaw
350-accept.text:
That Marzon would be contacting a member of the Defias and have ties to Lescovar...

Having killed VanCleef and Thredd, it would be hard to see Lescovar brought to proper justice, as your evidence is nothing without their testimonies. That is not even considering the fact that Lescovar is a noble and well connected. It effectively makes him above the law.

You'll need other help. I loathe to do so, but there is someone I know that will aid us. You'll find Trias in the Trade District of the city.
350-accept.title: Look to an Old Friend

350-complete.name: Elling Trias
350-complete.text:
You're kidding? Shaw wants my help again? Of all the nerve...

The Defias Brotherhood, you say? Well, you're certainly the bearer of wonderful news, aren't you? Next you're going to tell me that Deathwing is still alive and attacking the city.

All right, tell me everything from the beginning. And don't leave out something you think might not be important. I need to know it all.
350-complete.title: Look to an Old Friend

377-complete.name: Councilman Millstipe
377-complete.text: So Dextren Ward finally paid for his crimes against humanity?  Good riddance to the scum I say.  And cheers to you, my friend!  Not only have you given the families of the dead the peace of mind they deserve, you sent a poignant message to those corrupt bureaucrats in the House of Nobles.  Stormwind must rise to the needs of the people of Duskwood or we will break free from their tyranny.
377-complete.title: Crime and Punishment

377-progress.name: Councilman Millstipe
377-progress.text: So long as a molester of the dead like Dextren Ward is permitted to live, justice stands betrayed.  Return to me once Lord Ebonlocke's sentence of death is carried out on that defiler, Ward.  We shall give the families of the dead the closure they deserve and better yet, we will send a clear message to the House of Nobles in Stormwind.
377-progress.title: Crime and Punishment

386-complete.name: Guard Berton
386-complete.text: Targorr the Dread has finally met his fate.  I for one am glad to hear the beast now knows what it is like to be on the receiving end of Death's ruthless grip.  You have done well, $N.  Sometimes the truest justice can only be found outside the courtroom and beyond the clouded vision of politics.
386-complete.title: What Comes Around...

386-progress.name: Guard Berton
386-progress.text: Have you been to Stormwind yet, to The Stockade?  I fear whatever trickery that has kept Targorr the Dread alive for this long will eventually bring about his freedom.  He was sentenced to die, $N, not act as some political pawn on a noble's whim.
386-progress.title: What Comes Around...

387-accept.name: Warden Thelwater
387-accept.text:
The uprising must be quelled!  I need your assistance.  If word gets out that the prison is overrun I will lose my job!  This is a case of foul play if I've ever seen one.  But what's important now is forcing these prisoners into submission for the safety of Stormwind.

The punishment for insurgency is death.  Kill some of these deviants!  That ought to get things under control.
387-accept.title: Quell the Uprising

387-complete.name: Warden Thelwater
387-complete.text: Your efforts in The Stockade were valiant, $N.  It's obvious this problem is bigger than the both of us.  But you have performed well and for that I am thankful.
387-complete.title: Quell the Uprising

388-accept.name: Nikova Raskol
388-accept.text:
Bitterness flows through my veins like a cold river.  My grandson, Mac, was such a good boy.  A mere 14 years old.  When the army was sent off to the front, Mac took up arms to defend the city.  He was a guard in The Stockade, where the Defias gang is locked up.  Mac reprimanded some of the prisoners for tearing their wool blankets to make scarves, a symbol of their gang.  For that Mac was stabbed in the back.

I want revenge.  Bring me 10 of their precious Wool Bandanas.  They are the color of blood.
388-accept.title: The Color of Blood

388-complete.name: Nikova Raskol
388-complete.text:
So these bandanas -- filthy tokens of corruption -- are what my Mac had to die for?  Such a waste.  Such a tragic sacrifice. 

But alas, I cannot return to the past.  Just know, $N, that you have brought my family justice through your deeds.
388-complete.title: The Color of Blood

388-progress.name: Nikova Raskol
388-progress.text: I see you are back, $c.  Have you collected 10 Red Wool Bandanas from those Defias Scum in The Stockade yet?
388-progress.title: The Color of Blood

391-complete.name: Warden Thelwater
391-complete.text:
Without Thredd to lead them, hopefully the riots will be more controllable. We shall see.

I must say, after a half hour, I hardly expected you to come out, but it seems I misjudged you.

I'd guess, then, that you didn't get much useful information out of him? But I know a thing or two that might be of interest to you about Thredd's activities.
391-complete.title: The Stockade Riots

391-progress.name: Warden Thelwater
391-progress.text: Either you bring me Thredd's head, or I'll take yours, understand, $N?
391-progress.title: The Stockade Riots

392-accept.name: Warden Thelwater
392-accept.text:
During the first years of Thredd's imprisonment, he never had any visitors. I figured that he was no longer of use to the Brotherhood, so they abandoned him.

Anyway, a few months ago, that all changed; he started to get regular visits... once, maybe twice a week. It was a strange man--the quiet type. I had my suspicions, but all his papers checked out.

His documents claimed his name was Maelik; here's his description. I don't think he'll be coming to visit Thredd anymore.
392-accept.title: The Curious Visitor

392-complete.name: Baros Alexston
392-complete.text: Hmm. Maelik? No, the name doesn't sound familiar and neither does this description. But it could be anybody! A former Stonemason, one of the Defias Brotherhood... Though if he is as well connected as Thelwater suggests, perhaps someone else might recognize him. Let me think.
392-complete.title: The Curious Visitor

393-accept.name: Baros Alexston
393-accept.text:
I really haven't a clue, $N. There is someone else who might be able to help you, and it so happens that he owes me a favor for--well, let's not get into that. Master Mathias Shaw of SI:7 can be found in the barracks in Old Town. Shaw has his thumb on most of the shady, or underhanded dealings of the city.

If anyone knows, it'd be him.
393-accept.title: Shadow of the Past

393-complete.name: Master Mathias Shaw
393-complete.text:
What? What's this? Yes, I think I do know who this man is, but his name is not Maelik. Assassins wear many names and many masks, discarding them as they lose their usefulness. Another alias known to be used by this man is Marzon; though even that is surely not his true name.

Regardless, he is an assassin and I know a good deal about him.

Marzon is currently under the employ of Lord Gregor Lescovar, a lord of shady reputation, even given the corruption of the nobility of Stormwind.
393-complete.title: Shadow of the Past

393-progress.name: Master Mathias Shaw
393-progress.text: Greetings. Of what service can I be to you, $c?
393-progress.title: Shadow of the Past

401-accept.name: Sirra Von'Indi
401-accept.text: I'm almost finished translating that note.  If you come back in a few moments I should be done.
401-accept.title: Wait for Sirra to Finish

401-complete.name: Sirra Von'Indi
401-complete.text:
There we are.  It's translated...

<The air grows heavy, as if a thick, black curtain is drawn over the land...>
401-complete.title: Wait for Sirra to Finish

453-accept.name: Tavernkeep Smitts
453-accept.text:
Good luck, $N.  I hope you find the chap, and I hope you find him alive.

If he's left the safety of Darkshire then he could be prey to the beasts of the wilds.
453-accept.title: Finding the Shadowy Figure

453-complete.name: Jitters
453-complete.text:
<Jitters sighs...>

Yes, I'm the author of that book.  You finally found me, eh?

Well if you read that journal...then you only know the half of it!
453-complete.title: Finding the Shadowy Figure

453-progress.name: Jitters
453-progress.text: Who are you??  Leave me be!
453-progress.title: Finding the Shadowy Figure

463-accept.name: First Mate Fitzsimmons
463-accept.text:
You've heard of the Greenwarden? You're not looking for him, are you? Well I say you're crazy if you are, but who am I to keep a fool from his death?

If you are seeking that beast, then I hear he is in the marsh, east of the road where it forks to Dun Modr. He's lurking there among the crocs...and worse!

And leave your money here. You won't need it where you're going...and you don't want to chip ol' Greenie's tooth on your gold when he bites you in half, do you?
463-accept.title: The Greenwarden

538-accept.name: Milton Sheaf
538-accept.text:
$N.  If you don't mind a long journey then I have a task for you, to again help Stormwind fill its library.

The old kingdom of Alterac fell after the great war, and it had a large collection of books.  It's a tragedy that the city is ruined, but even more tragic is all of their knowledge lost!  We must recover what we can.

Southshore is the closest town to the Ruins of Alterac.  Go there and speak with Loremaster Dibbs.  He can direct you to the ruins, and to what books may be found there.
538-accept.title: Southshore

58-complete.name: Commander Althea Ebonlocke
58-complete.text: On behalf of the people of Darkshire and as the Leader of the Night Watch, I thank you, $N, for your bravery and dedication.  May the Light shine upon your ways.
58-complete.title: The Night Watch

95-complete.name: Unknown
95-complete.text: A mound of dirt is here, hastily piled up as if someone had need of hiding something...without much time to do it.
95-complete.title: Sven's Revenge

98-complete.name: Madame Eva
98-complete.text: I know, $N: Stalvan is dead.  I sensed a wave of hope ripple through the tainted forest.  Once and for all, Duskwood is free from his blood thirst.  My joy is hampered by thoughts of those who fell prey to the horrible beast.  Nonetheless, you are a brave and cunning $c.
98-complete.title: The Legend of Stalvan
